scalars.scalar_value: PhD or terminal Master’s degree preferred.

A minimum of ten (10) years of progressively responsible professional experience in higher education, human-centered design, innovation, entrepreneurship, or related fields, including substantial senior leadership experience. Candidates must demonstrate a proven track record of setting and executing strategy, leading multidisciplinary teams, managing significant budgets, building institutional partnerships, and driving organizational change. Demonstrated expertise in human-centered design through substantial professional practice, including user research, systems thinking, problem framing, synthesis, ideation, prototyping, and testing. Candidates should have the depth of knowledge and experience to establish standards of rigor, evaluate the quality of design work, and guide the development of human-centered design education and applied learning experiences. Prior leadership of a center or organization related to entrepreneurship, innovation, or a similar field is preferred. Meaningful involvement in fundraising efforts, including engagement with individual and institutional donors, is also preferred.

items.item_text: Bachelor's degree required; PhD or terminal Master’s degree preferred.

A minimum of ten (10) years of progressively responsible professional experience in higher education, human-centered design, innovation, entrepreneurship, or related fields, including substantial senior leadership experience. Candidates must demonstrate a proven track record of setting and executing strategy, leading multidisciplinary teams, managing significant budgets, building institutional partnerships, and driving organizational change. Demonstrated expertise in human-centered design through substantial professional practice, including user research, systems thinking, problem framing, synthesis, ideation, prototyping, and testing. Candidates should have the depth of knowledge and experience to establish standards of rigor, evaluate the quality of design work, and guide the development of human-centered design education and applied learning experiences. Prior leadership of a center or organization related to entrepreneurship, innovation, or a similar field is preferred. Meaningful involvement in fundraising efforts, including engagement with individual and institutional donors, is also preferred.

Lead The Hive’s strategic evolution as an integrated ecosystem for innovation, design, entrepreneurship, and experiential learning across The Claremont Colleges; unite stakeholders behind a clear mission and communicate its priorities.
Build a rigorous human-centered design curriculum with faculty and external experts: a progression of courses and applied experiences, clear outcomes, and increasing mastery.
Extend learning beyond coursework by connecting workshops, mentorship, projects, internships, and co-curricular experiences into accessible pathways.
Support student-led innovation with resources, expertise, community, and space while preserving ownership; help ideas become ventures, institutional or community initiatives, products, or services.
Build The Hive as a collaborative innovation studio through sustained, multi-year cross-sector and alumni partnerships addressing health care, sustainability, aging, technology, and higher education.
Advance responsible technology practice through experimentation with emerging tools and critical examination of implications for people, communities, institutions and the environment.

Align structure, staff, roles, resources and space; oversee operations, programs, communications, advancement, and a $1M–$1.5M budget; set and assess outcomes; engage College leadership, committees, 7Cs faculty and staff, employers, alumni and partners; build philanthropic support.
Reposition The Hive as a best-in-class resource for the 7Cs community.
Increase visibility for The Hive, reflected in strong outcome and engagement data.
Elevate the profile of the center in the eyes of prospective students and families, so that it becomes a point of attraction to the 7Cs.
Ensure The Hive contributes meaningfully to the wider value proposition of a unique college consortium.
Assess and evaluate new funding streams for the center itself, as well as for venture projects.
Depending on qualifications and experience, the Director may have teaching responsibilities.
